text: The centurion said, "Only speak a word." Jesus called receiving His word without His touch "great faith."
explanation:
A Roman centurion's servant lay paralysed and suffering. Jesus offered to come, but the centurion said, "I am not worthy that You should come under my roof. But only speak a word, and my servant will be healed. For I also am a man under authority." He recognised that Jesus had authority over sickness the way he had authority over soldiers. Jesus marvelled: "I have not found such great faith, not even in Israel!"

We're used to the laying on of hands, and that's good. But when you hear His word and believe it, without anyone touching you, Jesus calls that great faith. His word isn't limited by distance. As it goes forth, receive.

text: "Sin, taking opportunity by the commandment": the law becomes sin's base of operations. "Apart from the law sin was dead."
explanation:
Paul says he wouldn't have known covetousness "unless the law had said, 'You shall not covet.'" That's the Ten Commandments, the moral law. Then: "Sin, taking opportunity by the commandment, produced in me all manner of evil desire." The word for opportunity, aphorme, means a military base from which an attack is launched. "When the commandment came, sin revived and I died."

You've experienced it: the harder you try not to think about something, the more you think about it. The law is holy, just and good, but sin uses it as a launch pad. That's why "you are not under law but under grace." Not so you can sin, but so sin loses its base.

text: "He who condemns the righteous" is an abomination to the Lord. That includes condemning yourself.
explanation:
"He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the just, both of them alike are an abomination to the Lord." We understand that it's wrong for a sinner to justify himself. But if you're in Christ, you're righteous, and when you condemn yourself, you're condemning the righteous. In Hebrew, the word for condemn here comes from the same root as the word for wicked.

Hypocrisy is pretending to be what you're not. For a believer, acting like a sinner is the hypocrisy, not acting righteous. So pray bold prayers. Before you pray, say, "Father, You see me righteous. I am the righteousness of God in Christ."

text: In a theft dispute, the one who said "This is it" brought the case to God, and "whomever God condemns shall pay double."
explanation:
Under the law, if property went missing and someone said, "This is it" (literally, this is mine), both parties came before God, and "whomever the judges condemn shall pay double to his neighbour." But you can't say "This is mine" if you've been taught that healing, provision or the gifts of the Spirit aren't for today.

When the enemy steals your health, peace or finances, don't condemn yourself as if you're the one who deserves it. Come before the Father as the righteousness of God in Christ and say, "Healing is mine. Peace is mine." Then God condemns the thief, and the thief must restore double.

text: The Hebrew word for "stripes," makkah, is also used for plague. "By His stripes we are healed."
explanation:
The law limited a guilty man's beating to forty stripes. The word, makkah, also means a blow or plague, and Deuteronomy 28's curses use it for "extraordinary plagues… serious and prolonged sicknesses… every sickness and every plague." Jesus wasn't flogged under Jewish limits but by Romans, until "His visage was marred more than any man." He took the stripes the guilty deserved.

The curses of Deuteronomy 28 end with: "you shall be offered for sale… but no one will buy you." But Christ did. "Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law" (literally bought us out of the slave market) "having become a curse for us."

text: God measured the prodigal by the fatted calf, and the older brother by his own record.
explanation:
The son who rebelled and wasted everything came home to a robe, a ring, sandals and a feast. The son who stayed and boasted, "I never transgressed your commandment at any time," felt like he'd never received anything. Why? The father treated the prodigal according to the sacrifice, the fatted calf, a picture of Jesus. The older son insisted on his own righteousness, so that's what he was measured by.

Whose righteousness are you standing in? If it's Christ's, God treats you as He treats His Son, and nothing is withheld. If it's your own, you'll receive what your record deserves, which isn't much.

text: Jesus filled Peter's boat to sinking first. Then Peter fell at His knees and repented.
explanation:
Peter had fished all night and caught nothing. Jesus told him to let down his nets, and the catch was so great the nets began to break and both boats began to sink. Only then did Peter fall at Jesus' knees: "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord!" The goodness came before the repentance.

Sometimes God anoints you or blesses you on a day you know you don't deserve it, perhaps after a quarrel with your spouse. It's not because He approves of the quarrel. It's so you'll know His blessing was never about your performance. And that goodness is exactly what moves you to go home and make things right.
